$comment: Golden period-resolution cases, shared BYTE-IDENTICALLY by two test suites: the add-in's
Vitest suite and the gateway module's kotest suite.
Period resolution exists twice on purpose — the gateway is authoritative, and the add-in
keeps a local copy solely so the taskpane's period picker can show a resolved range
without a round trip per keystroke. Two implementations of the same rules drift SILENTLY:
both compile, both look right, and the only symptom is an interactive refresh and a 06:00
scheduled email covering different hours, each plausible on its own. This file is the
contract that makes that drift a red test instead of a support call.
Times are local wall-clock in `zone`. Both suites pin the process timezone to it, because
both resolvers deliberately use the AMBIENT zone — that is the real runtime behaviour, and
testing it any other way would test something we do not ship.
Cases marked xlreporter are verbatim from XLReporter's History Data Groups specification.

cases.name: relative current month, no start time
relative previous month, no start time
relative current day, start at 08:00, evaluated mid-shift
relative previous day, start at 08:00
before the daily start time the current period is still yesterday's
cases.note: 05:00 precedes the 08:00 shift start. Snapping naively to today 08:00 would report a period that has not begun.

cases.name: offset of zero matches the equivalent relative period
offset minus one day
offset minus one month keeps both the day of month and the duration
clamping turns current day into day-to-date
cases.note: The runtime rule that makes a template reusable: a schedule running daily returns 08:00 through now, growing as the shift proceeds, instead of a day of empty future intervals.

cases.name: a completed previous period is not clamped
month arithmetic clamps to a short month instead of overflowing
cases.note: Naive month addition turns 31 January into 3 March, and every end-of-month report drifts.

cases.name: a day across spring-forward keeps wall-clock time
cases.note: US DST begins 2026-03-08. Adding a fixed 24h of milliseconds would land at 09:00, and the shift report would silently cover 23 hours.

cases.name: a day across autumn fall-back keeps wall-clock time
cases.note: US DST ends 2026-11-01. This day is 25 hours long.

cases.name: aligned current day is day-to-date
cases.note: The period real reports mean by 'today'. Unaligned this is degenerate: start=now, and the clamp then pulls end back to now, giving an empty range.

cases.name: aligned previous day is yesterday, midnight to midnight
aligned current month is month-to-date
cases.note: Unaligned, XLReporter's own semantics make this a rolling month: 12 April to 12 May. Both are useful; only one is what 'this month' means.

cases.name: aligned previous month is the whole previous calendar month
aligned week starts on Monday
cases.note: ISO 8601. A real choice rather than an obvious one, so it is pinned here rather than left to the runtime. 2026-04-12 is a Sunday, whose ISO week began Monday the 6th.

cases.name: aligned quarter snaps to the first month of the quarter
aligned year snaps to 1 January
alignment and startAt combine: the month starting on the 1st at 06:00
cases.note: Snap to the unit boundary FIRST, then apply the time of day. Snapping afterwards would move the boundary to whichever day startAt last occurred on.

cases.name: an aligned boundary still ahead of now belongs to the period that has not begun
cases.note: The 1st at 03:00 with an 06:00 month start: the month underway began on 1 March, not 1 April.

cases.name: unaligned current month stays rolling, as XLReporter defines it
cases.note: Kept alongside the aligned case on purpose: both behaviours are correct and the flag is what chooses between them.

cases.name: absolute periods pass through untouched
